strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with interleaved local ops
strategies.desc: Performs 8 all-reduce operations sequentially, with local scaling/unscaling operations between each all-reduce. Each iteration does: scale by a[r], all-reduce, unscale by a[r]. This is the reference implementation pattern with 8 collective dispatches and O(W*S) local ops per stage, trading simplicity for dispatch count.

strategies.name: Fused local-op batching per all-reduce
strategies.desc: Pre-compute scale/unscale coefficients and fuse all local element-wise operations (scale, divide by W, unscale) into single vectorized kernels before/after each all-reduce. Reduces local-op dispatch overhead from 3W operations to 2W operations per stage (one fused scale+divide, one fused unscale), maintaining 8 collective dispatches but with better compute efficiency.

strategies.name: Pipelined reduce-scatter + all-gather chain
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing local scaling operations to overlap with the all-gather communication phase. Each of 8 stages becomes: reduce-scatter (get local shard), apply scale/unscale locally on smaller chunk, all-gather. Total 16 collective dispatches but smaller per-dispatch payload (S instead of W*S) and potential pipeline overlap.

strategies.name: Chunked ring-based manual all-reduce
strategies.desc: Manually implement all-reduce using send/recv primitives in a ring topology, chunking the W*S tensor into smaller segments. This allows interleaving local scaling operations with communication of different chunks, potentially hiding local compute latency. Each of 8 stages uses 2*(W-1) send/recv operations, higher dispatch count but fine-grained overlap opportunity.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level all-reduce with scale factorization
strategies.desc:
Exploit node structure by doing intra-node all-reduce first, then inter-node all-reduce, applying scaling transformations at the inter-node level only. For 8 stages with multi-node topology, performs 8 intra-node + 8 inter-node all-reduces (16 total collectives) but with smaller inter-node payloads and opportunity to pre-aggregate scaling factors within nodes to reduce redundant computation.
